title: Your Own Voice: Putting It Together

sections.content: This is the last lesson of B2. You do not learn a new form here. You choose among the tools you already have, and that choice is your own voice: what you say, how sure you are, and which register fits the person you are writing to. Here is a map of the tools of the last units.

sections.title: Your toolbox
rows: Estimado señor: Le escribo para pedirle información.
Choose the register: a formal letter (B2 Units 34 and 35).
El aumento de los precios preocupa a muchas familias.
Make a noun phrase the subject (B2 Unit 35).
Si bien es cierto que los salarios han subido, no han subido tanto como los precios.
Grant a point, then limit it (B2 Unit 35).
No cabe duda de que se necesitan medidas.
Say how sure you are (this unit).
Aprobada la ley, se espera que la situación mejore.
Compress with a participle clause (B2 Unit 35).
¿Quién puede negar que el problema es real?
Close with a rhetorical question (this unit).

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.content: A good short opinion text has four moves: say your point, give a reason, grant something to the other side, and finish. You do not need every tool in every text. A plain, correct sentence is better than a heavy one, and one device per paragraph is plenty. Read the example below as one paragraph: each sentence uses a different tool.

items.spanish: El aumento de los precios preocupa a muchas familias.
items.english: The rise in prices worries many families.

items.spanish: Si bien es cierto que los salarios han subido, no han subido tanto como los precios.
items.english: It is true that wages have risen, but not as much as prices.

items.spanish: No cabe duda de que se necesitan medidas.
items.english: There is no doubt that measures are needed.

items.spanish: ¿Quién puede negar que el problema es real?
items.english: Who can deny that the problem is real?

sections.content: Before you hand in a text, ask three questions. Is the register right for the reader (*tú* or *usted*)? Is each claim as sure as I want it to be? Does each paragraph have one clear point? That is B2 writing.
